issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' and a SealSaloon.stock attribute of type Stock, but the provided template and solution implement this concept in a class named 'Inventory'. The template even contains an empty Stock.java file. Concretely: the UML declares class Stock (problem_statement.md) and a SealSaloon->Stock association, while template/solution code defines public class Inventory with methods add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock and SealSaloon uses a static Inventory stock field. This mismatch between the identifier in the textual/UML specification ('Stock') and the actual code artifact ('Inventory') will confuse students about which class to modify or create and may lead to duplicate or inconsistent implementations or compilation issues if they follow the statement literally.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement and UML to refer to 'Inventory' everywhere (remove or repurpose the empty Stock.java), or (B) rename the Inventory class and its file to 'Stock' (rename Inventory.java to Stock.java and update all references, including SealSaloon) and delete the empty Stock.java file. Document the chosen name in the exercise text so students know which class to extend or modify.
